Original Taiwanese game art for "Tainan Gazetteer" (府城夜巡地圖), set in Tainan around 1930.
Style: handmade layered paper sculpture (紙雕 / kirie), the same for buildings, trees, plants,
fences, ground tiles, icons and props. Every shape is a piece of cut paper: visible paper fibres,
slightly soft hand-cut edges, pieces overlapping in shallow layers with small soft contact shadows
where one sheet sits on another. Colour is printed on the paper: clearly visible risograph /
stencil print grain and uneven ink density across every flat area, never a clean digital fill.
Weathering is welcome: irregular faded patches, not neat squares.
Details are built from few, large cut pieces (roof tiles, bricks, window frames, leaves, petals,
stones, planks), not painted lines and not crowded tiny patterns. Plants are natural and
asymmetric.
Colour: follow the real object, then mute it: pale, slightly greyed, warm. Typical tones: warm
cream, pale brick red, coral, sage and grey-green, mustard, indigo, wood brown, stone grey.
No saturated red-against-green contrast.
Buildings: strictly frontal elevation, no perspective, three or four flat paper layers.
Do NOT make: a 3D render or clay/plastic model, smooth bevelled relief, realistic or painterly
illustration, photo textures, thick foam layers, glow, glossy highlights, black outline strokes,
smooth gradients, depth of field.
Output: generated natively on a fully TRANSPARENT background (real alpha including enclosed
holes, no backdrop, no glow, no chroma-key colour, no coloured fringe), every object complete
and separated by clear transparent gutters, no ground, no base, no cast shadow outside the
object, no text, no captions, no logos.

Create only fences.png. Input images 1–2 are only paper texture and finish references, 3–4 only fence structure. Use original designs. Front-on landscape sprite sheet, exactly 4 equal columns and 2 equal rows, 8 isolated assets. In each column, top is one standalone centered post and bottom is its single matching full-cell-width connector, with no posts in bottom row. Top posts align at the baseline of their row. Bottom connectors extend flush to each horizontal cell boundary, with their ends positioned to meet the posts at corresponding heights when overlaying the two equal-sized cells. Column 1 fencePlank: slant-cut top on one pale weathered upright wooden plank, paired with one upper horizontal plank. Column 2 fenceCross: one chunky square timber post, paired with one X made from exactly two crossed flat pieces of wood; the four X ends reach the horizontal cell edges, the triangular gaps are transparent. Column 3 fenceRail: one slender rounded-top wooden stake, paired with exactly two thin parallel horizontal wood rails with plenty of transparent space between. Column 4 fenceBamboo: one vertical bamboo cane, paired with exactly two parallel slender horizontal bamboo canes with paper cord lashings near the ends. Muted varied timber tones and straw-sage bamboo. Clean native alpha. No scene, characters, icons, divisions or marks.
Critical geometry correction: first upper-left post must be ONLY a single uninterrupted slant-topped vertical plank. Never attach a horizontal crossbar there. Think unassembled, eight parts. Horizontal grid division exactly at 50% of total image height. All post feet land just above that horizontal division while remaining fully inside the upper half, with a clear transparent gap before the lower-row artwork. Reserve the upper half solely for those four isolated upright silhouettes. At lateral cell boundaries rails may touch the cell edge as specified, but ensure a hairline transparent separation between adjacent connectors of different styles. Use no additional wrap around the wooden posts.
